## bijection_verdict
**KB-BIJECTION PASS.** No omission, softening or addition. Retired surface: the four relevant overwritten clauses are shown as former clauses no longer in force with the clause now in force beside them; no undeclared retirement.

Source-side item (not a KB verdict), **XP-1**: the published Harborline Customer Accounts tier schedule (docs/account/tier_discount_schedule_71039551, terms 1–3, from blueprint account.yaml `account_tier_benefits`) states "A tier discount ... never applies to ... proration lines", "When a product's own promotion or volume discount could also apply to the same price component, only the single higher percentage applies; percentages are never added or compounded" and "Discounted components are rounded half up to the cent before fees are added". Both email policies of this task add the account-tier email discount to the seat-volume, hosting-bundle and domain rates into one combined rate, round once on the final figure (after the reinstatement charge is added), and apply the tier rate to the Pro upgrade line, which the tool books as charge_type `upgrade_proration`. No declared precedence covers this in-force base rule of another product (XF recipe item 17). The email documents state their own rules explicitly and the scored solution follows from them, but a reader who applies the account schedule gets other figures (e.g. reactivation with the single higher 6 %: 564.03, or 563.94 with the component rounded first). Nature: undeclared departure from another product's in-force base sentence.

### bijection_verdict (revision_2)
**KB-BIJECTION PASS.**

Source-side items (not KB verdicts):
- **SR-1** (seed realism): the three October `email_renewal_decline` rows (10-01, 10-05, 10-07) are seeded while the account credit stood at 73.35. Under the published rules, those attempts are term renewals billed on or before the due date: Starter scheduled with no upgrade line gives month-to-month 2.49, 17 or 16 renewed seats and Bronze 5 %, so about 40.21 / 37.85. Harborline Customer Accounts says "Every auto-renew charge in any category tries credit first", and the credit covers those amounts, so they would have been paid from credit and never declined. The task's own grounding text says "the renewal due exceeded the 73.35 account credit", which holds only at the retired current-product price (18 × 4.99 × 0.95 = 85.33).
- **BL-1** (baseline surface): the Pro upgrade rule defines the opening charge date as a plain binding: "The opening charge date is the charge date of the renewal charge that opened the current term ...; a fee is part of what that charge billed but never of what a term is credited". Only the two fee factors read it, but because it is a plain binding it falls to the computation document (pro_upgrade_charge_calculation item 8). There it is a quantity the baseline never uses, and its rationale signals that fees come off the credit, ahead of the fee factor documents. With "the credit basis less every fee taken off it" (baseline text) this is a factor-existence hint the renderer cannot avoid without dropping a rule sentence.

## revision_3
Source email.extended.yaml 86f1a705… (task_tools.py ff9caa38… unchanged); corpus 5da53262…; snapshot /tmp/erl0076_coord/kbsnap_professional_email_seats_r3.txt (DOCS OK, TRACEABILITY OK 0 misses, 7 gates OK); policy verdict revision_16 CLEAN.

### Round-2 items
- **BL-1 closed.** The Pro upgrade rule no longer has a plain opening-charge-date binding. The carried late-fee and carried reinstatement sentences each define "the charge date of the opening renewal charge (the renewal charge whose period start is the term start date)", within their own factor bindings (late_fee_days, suspended_days_then). pro_upgrade_charge_calculation has dropped item 8 and carries only the baseline rule; "opening charge date" occurs nowhere in the corpus. The baseline's own "less every fee taken off it ... no fee is taken off it" stays as baseline text (default-zero pattern).
- **SR-1 closed.** The ledger now holds a withdrawal of the full remaining balance (73.35) against the 2026-04-10 deposit on 2026-09-24, so the balance is 0.00 before the 10-01 / 10-05 / 10-07 attempts. Under "Every auto-renew charge in any category tries credit first ... otherwise the charge goes to the default card in full", each attempt goes to the card, and the declines are consistent. The withdrawal itself fits the published withdrawal rule: account active; inside the 180-day window (day 180 = 2026-10-07); amount = the deposit's withdrawable amount (no non-cash credit); at or above the 5.00 minimum; back to the card; first withdrawal against that deposit. The 500.00 deposit still counts toward the trailing-365-day Bronze minimum (withdrawals are not subtracted; only charge-backs are), so the tier stays Bronze, with no tier-review entry due (cycle 365 days from 2026-04-10).

### Cross-product re-judge (all seven corpora published)
The task world holds records in two products only: email and Harborline Customer Accounts. Domain, hosting, SSL, server and security return no records. Account rows: deposit 500.00 (card, 2026-04-10) qualifies Bronze the same day (business profile; 500.00 ≥ 500.00); five credit-first payments of 85.33 match the email term-renewal price as of each charge date (18 × 4.99 × 0.95, Bronze in force, no idle seats in those terms, nothing scheduled yet); withdrawal as above. Email rows: 79.84 new subscription and April renewal (16 × 4.99, Business account, 0 %); 5.99 added-seat proration (2 × 4.99 × 1 × 18/30; no tier discount on proration lines); all consistent with the published rules as of their dates.
